_comment: Platform agent — cross-cutting concerns. The defining constraint: production-safety. Mutating infra commands are blocked at the tool layer, not just by prompt discipline. See agents/platform/SPEC.md and CLAUDE.md.

modelOverrides._comment: Per-skill model routing. `conversational` is the lightweight default (architecture/deploy/cost Q&A + lookups + routing) — it produces no artifacts and doesn't load SYSTEM.md/ADR-index/dependency-graph, so it runs on Haiku at ~1/3 the token rates. A bare cold question (e.g. a Slack 'hello') drops from ~$0.25 (full architect procedure on Sonnet) to a few cents. Every artifact/decision skill (system-design/architect/devops/release-manager/finops/incident-response) stays on the default Sonnet-5 — architecture is judgment under trade-offs and reasoning depth matters most here of any agent.

costCap._comment: Cyrus pre-launch check enforces these. Project-scoped. Platform spans cheap work (cost reports, status) and expensive work (system-design — multi-session, big context). The per-job cap is set higher to accommodate system-design sessions. Incident-response is never throttled by off-hours. See agents/PROTOCOLS.md → Token / Cost Resilience Protocol.

allow: _note: allow is not a restriction today. The SDK treats allowedTools as auto-allowed without prompting and says to use the tools option to restrict, which the router does not set yet. So this list documents what the agent actually uses, and it becomes the real boundary the moment tools is wired from it. Write/Edit/TodoWrite are declared here because they were relied on but undeclared, or parked in ask, a tier nothing reads.

writeScope._comment: Platform writes: infra files + ADR/runbook/incident docs in target project + own state + version files. NEVER application code (Builders' territory), NEVER other agents' configs, NEVER deploy configs in production state. Note on enforcement, so this list is not mistaken for one: NOTHING in router/src reads allowedPaths — it documents intent. What actually stops a write is `permissions.deny` (which becomes the SDK's disallowedTools, removing the tool from the model's context) and a PreToolUse hook that denies. `permissions.allow` is NOT a boundary: the SDK's allowedTools only skips the permission prompt ("to restrict which tools are available, use the `tools` option instead"), the router never sets `tools`, and its canUseTool allows whatever no hook denies. Platform's Write/Edit sit in `permissions.ask`, which nothing reads, so they are available — bounded by the 72 deny entries and the block_if_path_matches hook below, not by this list.

SessionStart._comment: Always load: founding docs (the house-style preamble). NOT small, measured: the four founding docs are 99KB / ~25K tokens (PRODUCT.md alone is 46KB), cache-written on every session including the Haiku conversational ones. That predates the vault index below and is a separate scoping question — trimming what a light session needs from PRODUCT.md is its own change. Recorded here so the next reader does not trust the word "small". Plus the fleet-memory index — shared/README.md and shared/process/README.md, ~4KB / ~1K tokens of table-of-contents with wikilinks, NOT the notes themselves (harness-behavior.md alone is 9KB). Always-on because a vault nobody is told about is not memory: `shared/**` has been on this agent's git_commit paths since the tier was added and no config mentioned it, so the write path was open and the read path did not exist. Follow a wikilink and Read the one note you need — the state repo is already in the session's additionalDirectories. PROTOCOLS.md §8 (Fleet Memory Protocol) says when to read and where a lesson belongs.

Heavy context — SYSTEM.md + ADR index (Platform writes both — needs them to maintain consistency) + dependency-graph (architect's primary context) — loaded ONLY for the artifact/decision skills that use it. The lightweight `conversational` default skill (bare Q&A / lookups / routing) skips this so a one-line answer doesn't pay to cache-write tens-of-K tokens every session; it reads a specific ADR/SYSTEM.md section on demand instead. See load-hook `only_skills`.
If founding/STACK.md is missing, the architect skill cannot run productively. Refuse architecture work.
SessionStart.message: Phase 0 STACK.md is missing. Architecture work requires the stack context. Recommend `@strategist-agent kick off Phase 0` first.

PreToolUse._comment: Block any Write to application code, founding docs, or other agents' configs.
PreToolUse.message: Platform cannot modify application code, founding docs, or other agents' configs. Bounce this to the appropriate Builder or Strategist agent.

PreToolUse._comment: Production-safety gate on Bash. The deny patterns above are the technical enforcement. If a command tries to bypass — e.g. constructing the deny-listed string at runtime — this hook re-checks the final invocation.
PreToolUse.on_block_message: 🛑 Production-safety rule: this command would mutate real infrastructure. I cannot execute it. The plan/proposal goes to a human for approval and execution. See `dev-team/agents/platform/CLAUDE.md` → 'The production-safety rule'.

PreToolUse.message: Platform does not merge PRs — including its own infra PRs. Blast radius requires human review.

_implementationNotes.production_safety: The deny list is the most important part of this settings file. Every mutating infra command pattern across major tools (Terraform, Pulumi, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, AWS CLI, gcloud, deploy tools, curl mutations) is in the deny list. The PreToolUse hook re-checks the final command string in case the agent constructs the command dynamically.
_implementationNotes.model: Sonnet with extended thinking — architecture is judgment under trade-offs; reasoning depth matters most here of any agent.
_implementationNotes.writeScope: Reads everything (architect mandate). Writes narrowly to infra files + docs + own state. Application code and other agents' configs are denied. Enforcement is the deny list + PreToolUse hooks, not allowedPaths (which nothing reads) and not permissions.allow (which only skips the prompt).
mcp_servers_required: anthropic-usage (for FinOps watching agent fleet spend)
future_additions: Pre-authorized rollback exception: per Platform SPEC §12 q2, consider a tightly-scoped opt-in where the agent may execute a rollback to the immediately-previous known-good version IF a human has pre-authorized rollback-only for that service. Not in initial settings; revisit after first 90 days of operation.
